simple.meaning: חַת (chath) is a Hebrew action word meaning “concretely, crushed ; also afraid ; abstractly, terror.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 5 times in Genesis, 1 Samuel, Job, Isaiah, Jeremiah, beginning at Genesis 9:2. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חַת (H2844) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: חַת (chath) / H2844 is traced through Genesis 9:2, 1 Samuel 2:4, Job 41:25, Isaiah 7:8 with source-language evidence and verse context.

occurrences.englishText: The fear of you and the dread of you will be on every animal of the earth, and on every bird of the sky. Everything that moves along the ground, and all the fish of the sea, are delivered into your hand.
“The bows of the mighty men are broken.
When he raises himself up, the mighty are afraid.
For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin. Within sixty-five years Ephraim shall be broken in pieces, so that it shall not be a people.
